answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake bonded to verifiable work history. Each agent locks a deposit and earns reputation through attested completed tasks, accruing slowly, like pigment settling into a grove of trees at dawn. A new identity starts with zero standing and cannot borrow another's history. An attacker minting thousands of fakes must fund a deposit for each, do work to earn trust, and risks losing every deposit if random audits catch coordinated fraud. Forging identities stays cheap, but making them trusted is expensive, so flooding no longer pays.
